query: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Micro-alloying equiatomic NbMoTaW with a small addition (≈5 at.%) of V (producing (NbMoTaW)95V5) will increase room-temperature tensile ductility (>5 % uniform elongation vs. <1 % in the baseline alloy) while retaining ≥90 % of the 1600 °C yield strength and exhibiting equal or lower irradiation-induced hardening after 2 dpa heavy-ion exposure at 600 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic NbMoTaW high-entropy alloy processed to a single-phase BCC solid solution; grain size 10–30 µm; no prior cold work.
generation.intervention: Add 5 atomic % vanadium, homogenize at 1400 °C for 24 h and water-quench to preserve a single-phase BCC solid solution (composition (NbMoTaW)95V5).
generation.conditions: Mechanical tests: (i) room temperature (25 °C) and (ii) 1600 °C in Ar atmosphere, strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Irradiation test: 1 MeV Kr²⁺ ions to 2 dpa at 600 °C, followed by nano-indentation at 25 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Uniform substitutional V atoms in the BCC lattice reduce the average shear modulus and Peierls barrier, facilitating dislocation glide; high configurational entropy and similar atomic size preserve single-phase stability.
generation.mechanism: 1. V atoms (lower shear modulus and lattice friction than Nb/Mo/Ta/W) soften the lattice, lowering the critical resolved shear stress and enabling easier dislocation nucleation and motion at 25 °C, thereby increasing ductility. 2. Solid-solution strengthening from size and modulus mismatch, combined with sluggish diffusion, sustains high strength at 1600 °C despite slight softening. 3. High chemical disorder and comparable vacancy formation energies of V maintain efficient point-defect recombination, so irradiation-induced defect accumulation and hardening remain unchanged or decrease slightly.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the untreated alloy: • Room-temperature: uniform elongation increases from <1 % to >5 %; yield strength decreases ≤15 %. • 1600 °C: yield strength ≥90 % of baseline; creep rate unchanged within experimental scatter. • Irradiation: nano-indentation hardness increase after 2 dpa ≤ baseline (±10 %).
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic NbMoTaW: ~0.5–1 % RT elongation, high yield strength at RT (~1.4 GPa) and at 1600 °C (~350 MPa), irradiation hardening ΔH ≈ +0.6 GPa after 2 dpa Kr ±600 °C (literature values).
generation.boundary: Valid for single-phase BCC (NbMoTaW)100−xVx alloys with 0 ≤ x ≤ 8 at.% processed without secondary phase precipitation; tests at strain rates 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹ and temperatures ≤1600 °C. Outside this range, precipitation or excessive solid-solution softening may alter outcomes.
generation.uncertainty: No direct experimental data yet exist for V-doped NbMoTaW; predicted magnitudes assume linear rule-of-mixtures effects on elastic constants and Peierls stress. Excess V or slower quench rates could form Laves or σ phases, degrading properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize 30 g ingots of NbMoTaW (baseline) and (NbMoTaW)95V5 via arc melting + drop casting. Homogenize 1400 °C/24 h/WQ. Machine dog-bone specimens. Perform: (1) tensile tests at 25 °C and 1600 °C (10⁻³ s⁻¹); (2) creep at 1600 °C, 200 MPa for 100 h; (3) 1 MeV Kr²⁺ irradiation to 2 dpa at 600 °C, measure nano-indentation hardness depth profiles (500 nm).
measurements: RT yield strength and uniform elongation
TEM characterization of defect density and secondary phases
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if any of the following occur: (a) RT uniform elongation increase <3 % absolute; (b) 1600 °C yield strength drops >10 % relative to baseline; (c) ΔH after irradiation exceeds baseline by >10 %; (d) secondary phases detected (>2 vol %).
